( 57 ) ABSTRACT
An epitaxial deposition process , such as atomic layer depo sition , is provided for forming a thin film comprising beta gallium oxide ( ß - Ga203 ) on a substrate , such as sapphire . The process involves depositing a buffer layer of metastable Ga_O3 , such as a - Ga , 03 , on the substrate , and then reacting a gallium precursor , such as TEG , with an oxygen precursor , such as oxygen plasma , to deposit a layer comprising B - Ga203 on the buffer layer . The Ga2O3 film formed by the process may comprise highly oriented crystalline ß - Ga , 03 , with negligible amounts of other Gazoz polymorphs .

FIELD OF THE INVENTION
[ 0002 ] The present invention relates to forming semicon ductor thin films , using epitaxial deposition processes .

Otherwise , post - growth annealing at high temperatures ( > 500 ° C. ) will be required to achieve a high quality film [ Reference no . 7 ] .
[ 0007 ] In addition to B - Ga2O3 , which is the most stable polymorph of Ga203 , gallium oxide has a few other poly morphs that are metastable ; these include Y- , E- , K- , d- , and a - Ga_03 [ References no . 3 , 9-14 ] . Currently , the y poly morphs can only be obtained in specific process conditions ; meanwhile , information about the ? , K , and 8 polymorphs is
limited and , in some cases , debated in the literature [ Refer ences no . 11 , 12 ] mainly because these polymorphs are difficult to obtain as isolated phases which makes their structure determination challenging [ Reference no . 7 ] . On the other hand , the a - Ga203 metastable polymorph is the most studied and technologically appealing metastable poly morph due to its superior properties for both power handling and optoelectronics and its stability at ambient to high temperatures and pressures [ References no . 3 , 7 , 9 , 10 ) .
[ 0008 ] There remains a need in the art for methods for forming a high quality , thin film comprising B - Ga Oz on a non - native substrate , using an energy - efficient fabrication
process .

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
[ 0003 ] Power electronic devices are devices that convert DC power to AC power , or vice versa . For example , power electronic devices convert DC power generated by solar cells and fuel cells to AC power , thereby making it usable by consumers . As another example , power electronic devices convert AC power supplied by a provider to DC power , thereby making it usable for charging the battery of an
electric car or a portable electronic device . [ 0004 ] Research into new materials for power electronic devices has emerged as an inseparable part of sustainable development and efficient handling of electrical energy during the past three decades . Wide bandgap semiconduc tors such as GaN and SiC have been considered as candidate
materials for power devices to overcome the limitations of their traditional predecessors ( such as Si and GaAs ) in meeting the growing needs and the stringent requirements of the high energy demand society today . [ 0005 ] During the past few years , gallium oxide ( Ga , 02 ) has been proposed as an alternative material for such semi conductor devices promising to offer higher efficiency in power handling than the materials in use today and expected to compete with and complement the outstanding properties of GaN as the frontrunner material for power electronic devices [ References no . 1-5 ] . In addition to power applica tions , Ga , 0 , expands the wavelength span of optoelectronic devices to the deep UV [ Reference no . 3 ] . The properties of Gazoz depend on its crystal structure [ Reference no . 3 ) , and high quality films of crystalline forms of Ga203 , specifically of its most stable polymorph , are required for fabricating devices .
[ 0006 ] Therefore , most attention has been devoted to monoclinic ß - Ga203 as the most stable polymorph of Ga203 ( belonging to the space group C2 / m ) . With the recent availability of ß - Ga203 bulk wafers ( grown from the melt at high temperatures , ca. 1800 ° C. ) [ References no . 1 , 3-5 ] , homoepitaxial thin films of this Ga203 polymorph can be deposited on its native substrate [ References no . 1 , 3 , 4 ] . However , growing high quality B - Gazoz films on the native substrate ( i.e. , homoepitaxy ) is currently performed at high temperatures , ca. 600-800 ° C. , which consumes a lot of energy , and still only produces B - Ga_02 films on B - Ga_02 wafers that only allow for fabrication of very limited devices for limited applications [ References no . 1 , 2 ] . In addition , bulk B - Gazoz wafers have a low thermal conductivity which hinders the ability of ß - Ga203 devices to operate at their expected capabilities [ Reference no . 6 ] . Meanwhile , grow ing ß - Ga203 films on non - native substrates ( i.e. , heteroepi taxy ) is even more challenging ; it is only possible on very
[ 0009 ] The present invention involves using an epitaxial deposition process , such as plasma - enhanced atomic layer deposition , to form an intermediate buffer layer of a meta stable Ga2O3 , such as a - Ga2O3 , before depositing reactants that form the B - Ga_03 film on the buffer layer . In embodi ments , the process may be optimized to achieve crystallinity at a temperature of about 277 ° C. which is relatively low in the context of crystalline material growth . In embodiments , the process provides an energy - efficient fabrication process for growing ß - Ga203 films , with minimal inclusion of other Ga203 polymorphs , on non - native substrates on which an intermediate layer of metastable Gazoz can be grown .
[ 0010 ] In one aspect , the present invention comprises a method for forming a thin film comprising beta - gallium oxide ( ß - Ga203 ) on a substrate . The method uses an epi taxial deposition process comprising the steps of :
[ 0011 ] ( a ) depositing a buffer layer of metastable Gazoz on the substrate ; and
[ 0012 ] ( b ) reacting a gallium precursor with an oxygen precursor to deposit a layer comprising ß - Ga_03 on the buffer layer .
[ 0013 ] In embodiments of the method , the method further comprises repeating step ( b ) to deposit one or more addi tional layers comprising B - Ga Oz on a previously deposited layer comprising B - Ga_03 .
[ 0014 ] In embodiments of the method , the layer compris ing B - Gazoz comprises at least 90 % B - Ga2O3 , by ratio of mass of ß - Ga202 to mass of a - Ga203 and B - Ga203 , collec tively .
[ 0015 ] In embodiments of the method , the epitaxial depo sition process is an atomic layer deposition ( ALD ) process .
[ 0016 ] In embodiments of the method , the buffer layer is a single monolayer of metastable Ga203 . In embodiments of the method , the layer comprising B - Ga203 is a single mono layer comprising B - Ga203 .

[ 0043 ] " Atomic layer deposition ” or “ ALD ” is a subclass of chemical vapor deposition , used to deposit thin films onto a substrate . ALD typically involves the sequential use of gas phase reactants , and / or plasma phase reactants , and surface chemical processes .
[ 0044 ] “ Buffer layer " is one or more material layer ( s ) that provide an interface between a substrate underlying the buffer layer and an overlying film formed on the buffer layer .
[ 0045 ] “ Epitaxial deposition process ” , as used herein , refers to a process that involves placing a substrate in a reaction chamber , and introducing one or more precursor ( reactant ) materials into the reaction chamber , such that the precursor ( s ) or their reaction product ( s ) , deposit on the substrate to form a non - amorphous , crystalline layer having defined crystallographic orientation ( s ) relative to the under lying layer ( s ) . In non - limiting embodiments , the epitaxial deposition process may comprise chemical vapor deposition ( CVD ) processes , physical vapor deposition ( PVD ) pro cesses , or any other suitable deposition techniques as are known to a person skilled in the art of forming thin films . Chemical vapor deposition ( CVD ) processes may be per formed using a variety of techniques known to a person skilled in the art , with non - limiting embodiments including metal - organic CVD ( MOCVD ) , mist CVD , low pressure CVD , atmospheric CVD , plasma - assisted CVD ( also referred to as plasma - enhanced CVD ) , photo - assisted CVD , molecular layer deposition ( MLD ) , and atomic layer depo sition ( ALD ) including spatial ALD , thermal ALD , plasma assisted ALD ( also referred to as plasma - enhanced ALD ) , and photo - assisted ALD . Metal - organic vapor phase epitaxy ( MOVPE ) , halide vapor phase epitaxy ( HVPE ) and liquid phase epitaxy ( LPE ) may also be used . Physical vapor deposition ( PVD ) processes may be performed using a variety of sputtering techniques known to a person skilled in the art , with non - limiting embodiments including ion beam deposition , reactive sputtering , magnetron sputtering , and RF diode sputtering . Physical vapor deposition ( PVD ) pro cesses may also be performed using a variety of evaporation techniques known to a person skilled in the art , with non - limiting embodiments including thermal evaporation , e - beam evaporation , pulsed laser deposition ( PLD ) , and molecular beam epitaxy ( MBE ) including reactive MBE .
[ 0046 ] “ Gallium precursor ” , as used herein , refers to a substance comprising gallium atoms , which is suitable for use as reactant in an epitaxial deposition process . Method of the Present Invention
[ 0053 ] FIG . 1 is a schematic depiction of steps in an embodiment of the method of present invention for forming a thin film comprising B - Ga203 . This method is referred to herein as the “ buffer - mediated Ga203 deposition process ” . In one embodiment , the buffer - mediated Ga , O3 deposition process uses an epitaxial deposition process comprising the following steps :
[ 0054 ] ( a ) depositing a buffer layer of metastable Ga_03 on a substrate ; [ 0055 ] ( b ) reacting a gallium precursor ( e.g. , triethylgal lium ( TEG ) gas ) with an oxygen precursor ( e.g. , oxygen plasma ) to deposit a layer of B - Ga O , on the buffer layer ;
and
[ 0056 ] ( c ) repeating step ( b ) to deposit additional layers of B - Ga , 0 , on previously deposited layers of ß - Ga , 03 .
[ 0057 ] In one non - limiting embodiment , the substrate is a GaN - compatible substrate . In one embodiment , the GaN compatible substrate is sapphire , and more particularly c - plane sapphire . Abundant data is available for depositing Ga_03 and relevant materials on sapphire [ References no . 7 , 15 , 17 , 18 ] . [ 0058 ] Step ( a ) : Depositing Buffer Layer of Metastable
Ga203 . [ 0059 ] In general , step ( a ) may be performed by any epitaxial deposition process that can produce metastable Ga_03 on the substrate . In embodiments , the metastable Ga , 0 may be any one of the a - Ga , 03 , Y - Ga , 03 , E - Ga , 03 , K - Ga , 03 , and 8 - Gazoz polymorphs . For example , in embodiments where the metastable Ga203 is a - Ga203 , epi taxial deposition processes for forming a - Ga203 on a sub strate known in the art may be suitably used in the present

a - Ga203 on the substrate ( step 204 ) ; and [ 0065 ] ( c ) repeating the foregoing steps ( a ) and ( b ) ( see steps 206 to 210 , and 212 ) to deposit additional layers of a - Ga203 on previously deposited layer ( s ) of a - Ga2O3 .
[ 0066 ] In embodiments of the GaN - mediated a - Ga203 deposition process , the epitaxial deposition process is plasma - enhanced ALD .
[ 0067 ] In embodiments of the GaN - mediated a - Ga203 deposition process , each deposited layer of w - GaN , gallium
precursor , and nitrogen precursor , and a - Ga2O3 is a mono layer .
[ 0068 ] In embodiments of the GaN - mediated a - Ga203 deposition process , the process may be performed at a deposition temperature less than about 500 ° C. , and prefer ably less than about 300 ° C. , such as 277 ° C.
[ 0069 ] In embodiments of the GaN - mediated a - Ga_03 deposition process , step ( a ) is preceded by pretreating the
substrate with N / H , forming gas plasma to remove con tamination and pretreat the surface prior to deposition .
[ 0070 ] In embodiments of the GaN - mediated a - Ga 03 deposition process , sub - steps ( a ) ( i ) and ( a ) ( ii ) and step ( b ) may comprise providing pulsed doses of the gallium pre cursor , nitrogen precursor and oxygen precursor , respec
tively , into the reaction chamber in which the epitaxial deposition process is performed .
[ 0071 ] In embodiments of the GaN - mediated a - Ga203 deposition process , introduction of the gallium precursor and the nitrogen precursor into the reaction chamber is sequential , and the nitrogen precursor reacts with the first gallium precursor layer on the surface of the substrate . In other embodiments ( e.g. , using chemical vapor deposition ) , the introduction of the gallium precursor and the nitrogen precursor into the reaction chamber may be simultaneous to form the first layer of w - GaN on the substrate . In either case , the formed layer of w - GaN provides a highly symmetric atomic scale scaffold of gallium atoms , but is sacrificed in the following step to form the layer of a - Ga203 on the
substrate .
[ 0072 ] In embodiments of the GaN - mediated a - Ga203 deposition process , any one of sub - steps ( a ) ( i ) or ( a ) ( ii ) or step ( b ) may be followed by purging the reaction chamber in which the epitaxial deposition process is performed with an inert gas ( e.g. , argon gas ) to remove any excess of the gallium precursor , nitrogen precursor , or oxygen precursor ( as the case may be ) and / or reaction byproducts from the
reaction chamber .
[ 0073 ] As demonstrated by the experiment example described below , the GaN - mediated a - Ga203 deposition process is advantageous because it can be performed using GaN - compatible substrates , and is able to produce a very high quality , highly oriented , metastable a - Ga buffer layer .
[ 0074 ] Step ( b ) : Depositing B - Ga 03 Layer on Buffer Layer .
[ 0075 ] In general , step ( b ) may be performed by any epitaxial deposition process that involves reacting a gallium precursor with an oxygen precursor to deposit a layer of Ga203 on the buffer layer . This process is referred to herein as the " Ga 0 , deposition process " .
[ 0076 ] In one non - limiting embodiment as shown in part of FIG . 8 , the Ga Oz deposition process uses an epitaxial deposition process comprising the following steps :
[ 0077 ] ( a ) depositing a layer of triethylgallium ( TEG ) gas on the buffer layer ; [ 0078 ] ( b ) reacting the layer of TEG with oxygen plasma to deposit a layer of Ga203 on the buffer layer ; and [ 0079 ] ( c ) repeating the foregoing steps ( a ) and ( b ) to create additional layers of Ga Oz on previously deposited layer ( s ) of Ga203 . [ 0080 ] In embodiments of the Ga203 deposition process , epitaxial deposition process is plasma - enhanced ALD . [ 0081 ] In embodiments of the Ga203 deposition process , each deposited layer of TEG , oxygen plasma , and Ga203 is a monolayer .
[ 0082 ] In embodiments of the Ga203 deposition process , the process may be performed at a deposition temperature less than about 500 ° C. , and preferably less than about 300 ° C. , such as 277 ° C.
[ 0083 ] In embodiments of the Ga203 deposition process , step ( a ) may be preceded by pretreating the substrate with oxygen plasma to remove contamination and pretreat the surface prior to deposition . [ 0084 ] In embodiments of the Ga2O3 deposition process , steps ( a ) and ( b ) comprise providing pulsed doses of TEG and the oxygen plasma , respectively , into the reaction cham ber in which the epitaxial deposition process is performed . [ 0085 ] In embodiments of the Ga203 deposition process , any one of steps ( a ) or ( b ) may be followed by purging the reaction chamber in which the epitaxial deposition process is performed with an inert gas ( e.g. , argon gas ) to remove any excess of the TEG , or oxygen plasma , and / or reaction byproducts from the reaction chamber .

[ 0098 ] FIG . 3 shows the XRD results for an ~ 22 nm film of metastable a - Ga 03 deposited on C - plane sapphire ( a - A1,0z ) using the GaN - mediated a - Ga 02 deposition method . An intense peak for a - Ga203 ( 006 ) is observed right next to the a - A1203 ( 006 ) peak . No other peaks from a - Ga203 are present in the pattern which indicates that the a - Ga203 film is a highly oriented film with a - Ga203 ( 006 ) planes oriented parallel to the surface . Meanwhile , ß - Ga203 peaks are hardly detectable , which is indicative of their low population in the film . [ 0099 ] FIGS . 4 to 6 show the transmission electron microscopy ( TEM ) results for the same ~ 22 nm film of metastable a - Ga203 . These figures , particularly the atomic resolution STEM image in FIG . 4 , confirm that the entire film ( ~ 22 nm ) is crystalline and that the crystal structure is predominantly a - Ga203 such that a - Ga203 ( 006 ) planes are parallel to the surface . In FIGS . 5 and 6 , these results are confirmed from the distinct and intense diffraction spots in the electron diffraction patterns of focused regions of the film and the substrate , respectively .
[ 0100 ] FIG . 7 shows the out - of - plane XRD scan results for the Ga2O3 film deposited directly on the substrate using the conventional Ga203 deposition process . The Ga203 film studied in FIG . 7 had a thickness of -39.5 nm . From the
intense peaks from a - Gazoz ( 006 ) planes as well as B - Ga , Oz ( 201 ) family of planes parallel to the surface , it is evident that the Gazoz film is a mixture of a - Ga , O3 and B - Ga203 .
[ 0101 ] FIG . 8 shows the out - of - plane XRD scan results for the Ga203 film deposited on the buffer layer , in accordance with the buffer - mediated Ga_03 deposition process of the present invention . The Ga203 film studied in FIG . 8 consists of ~ 3 nm layer of a - Ga203 as the buffer layer , overlaid by an ~ 27.5 nm layer of Ga203 as the bulk of the film . In contrast to the conventional Ga203 deposition process , the buffer - mediated Ga_03 deposition process produces a sub stantially single phase B - Gazoz film . In FIG . 8 , three intense peaks from B - Ga , 03 ( 201 ) family of planes are observed parallel to the surface . More specifically , moving from low to high 20 angles in FIG . 8 , these B - Ga , 03 peaks correspond to B - Ga203 ( 201 ) , B - Ga203 ( 402 ) , and B - Ga2O3 ( 603 ) planes , respectively . [ 0103 ] Based on in - situ ellipsometry measurements , after 450 doses of gallium precursor ( i.e. , triethylgallium or TEG in this instance ) for depositing the film under study , the reference a - Ga_03 film deposited by using the GaN - medi ated Ga203 deposition process ( FIG . 3 ) had a thickness of -22 nm , the reference a - Ga 03 / B - Ga , 03 mixed - phase Ga203 film deposited by using the conventional Ga203 deposition process ( FIG . 7 ) had a thickness of ~ 26 nm , and the B - Ga_0 , film deposited by using the buffer - mediated Ga2O3 deposition process ( FIG . 8 ) of the present invention had a thickness of ~ 27.5 nm . The difference in thickness of
the Ga203 films despite using the same 450 TEG doses ( i.e. , constant Ga content in the films ) is consistent with the fact that ß - Ga 03 has a larger molar volume than a - Ga203 [ References no . 9 , 10 ] . Thus , an increase in the amount of B - Ga203 phase present in the film results in a thicker film for
a constant number of TEG doses . Accordingly , with a constant number of TEG doses , the Ga Oz film deposited by using the buffer - mediated Ga2O3 deposition process has the largest thickness among all films confirming the largest population of ß - Ga2O3 in this film .
[ 0104 ] In addition to crystal structure , investigating opti cal properties of the thin films can provide insights into the quality and performance of the material . To that end , in - situ ellipsometry measurements performed on the aforemen
tioned films ( i.e. , after the same 450 TEG doses ) were also used to study their optical properties . FIG . 9 shows the results of these studies in terms of values of extinction
coefficient ( k ) , refractive index ( n ) , and bandgap for the three Ga203 films .
[ 0105 ] As shown in FIG . 9 , using the GaN - mediated a - Ga , 0 , deposition process ( FIG . 3 ) results in an a - Ga , 03 film with largest refractive index values among the three films over the entire measured spectral range . This obser vation is consistent with the crystal structure of the films noting that a - Ga203 has a higher atomic packing density
( i.e. , smaller molar volume ) than B - Ga203 , and thus is expected to have a larger refractive index compared to the R phase [ References no . 9 , 10 ] .
[ 0106 ] As shown in FIG . 9 , specifically at the photon energy of 1.96 eV ( equivalent to 632.8 nm ) at which light absorption does not occur in gallium oxide ( i.e. , k = 0 at 632.8 nm ) , the ß - Ga203 film deposited by using the buffer - medi ated Ga_03 deposition process ( FIG . 8 ) has the lowest refractive index value among the three films while the a - Ga , 0 , film produced by the GaN - mediated a - Ga_03 deposition process ( FIG . 3 ) has the highest refractive index value . Moreover , the c - Ga_03 / B - Ga , 03 mixed - phase Ga 03 film deposited using the conventional Ga_03 deposition process ( FIG . 7 ) has a refractive index value between the
single - phase films . This is consistent with the fact that the conventionally deposited film comprises of a and B - Ga203 phases .
[ 0107 ] FIG . I also shows that the B - Ga_03 film deposited by using the buffer - mediated Ga203 deposition process ( FIG . 8 ) has the lowest bandgap value compared to the other films , and the value of bandgap increases as the a - Ga_03 content increases in the film with the GaN - mediated a - Ga 03 film having the highest bandgap value . These
observations are consistent with literature reports for band gap values of a and B - Ga203 [ Reference no . 3 ] and further confirm the purity of ß - Ga_03 phase in the film deposited by using the buffer - mediated Ga203 deposition approach of the present invention . Based on FIG . 9 , the values of extinction coefficient ( k ) for the Ga203 films are similar to each other . Meanwhile , compared to the other films , the B - Ga 03 film deposited by using the buffer - mediated Ga203 deposition process ( FIG . 8 ) has a generally larger extinction coefficient ( k ) in non - zero regions of the dispersion curves of k which is indicative of a larger concentration of free carriers in the conduction band of the B - Ga203 film after the free carriers have been excited to the conduction band by photons having high - enough energy [ see Reference no . 7 for further expla nation ] [ 0108 ] Without restriction to a theory , the foregoing results — i.e . , the high purity of ß - Ga , 03 phase in the film deposited by using the buffer - mediated Gazoz deposition approach may be attributed to the fact that depositing dominantly metastable gallium oxide as an intermediate buffer layer on the substrate before performing the conven tional Ga 03 deposition process increases the free energy of
the system which makes the formation of ß - Ga203 in the subsequently overlying film more favorable when perform ing the conventional Ga203 deposition process on such a high energy underlying template . [ 0109 ] In summary , the present invention provides an epitaxial deposition process that allows for formation of a highly oriented , crystalline B - Ga203 film on a substrate , which may even be a non - native substrate ( and more par ticularly , a GaN - compatible substrate ) at a low thermal budget ( i.e. , at temperatures that are hundreds of degrees lower than the processes currently in use for B - Ga_03 deposition ) .
[ 0110 ] The experimental results demonstrate that this buf fer - mediated Ga 0 , deposition process ( FIG . 8 ) may mini mize the formation of non - ß - Ga_03 polymorphs , and hinder formation of a mixed - phase material of ß - Ga203 with other polymorphs , as is produced by the reference conventional Ga 0 , deposition process ( FIG . 7 ) at the same deposition temperature and conditions , but which does not involve forming the buffer layer . Accordingly , the crystalline Ga_03 film formed by the present invention may be predominantly of the ß - Ga 03 polymorph , with minimal inclusion of other Ga203 polymorphs . [ 0111 ] The present invention makes the development of Ga203 semiconductor heterostructures and integration of Ga , 03 with existing semiconductor device components on a monolithic substrate possible and facilitates fast - track devel opment of Ga_02 electronics . Development of a low tem perature technology for B - Ga , 03 growth ( specially a GaN compatible one ) as a result of the present invention is a key enabling technology for wide bandgap semiconductors lead ing to energy - efficient electronic devices , not only in per formance but also an energy - efficient fabrication process . Fabrication of Ga203 devices on non - native substrates using the present invention also allows for the transfer of pertinent thermal management technologies that are already estab
lished for wide bandgap electronics [ Reference no . 16 ) , which will mitigate the low thermal conductivity of Ga_03 and make devices available that are able to concurrently handle higher power , higher voltage , and higher operating temperatures .

( 57 ) ABSTRACT
An epitaxial deposition process , such as atomic layer depo sition , is provided for forming a thin film comprising beta gallium oxide ( ß - Ga203 ) on a substrate , such as sapphire . The process involves depositing a buffer layer of metastable Ga_O3 , such as a - Ga , 03 , on the substrate , and then reacting a gallium precursor , such as TEG , with an oxygen precursor , such as oxygen plasma , to deposit a layer comprising B - Ga203 on the buffer layer . The Ga2O3 film formed by the process may comprise highly oriented crystalline ß - Ga , 03 , with negligible amounts of other Gazoz polymorphs .

FIELD OF THE INVENTION
[ 0002 ] The present invention relates to forming semicon ductor thin films , using epitaxial deposition processes .

Otherwise , post - growth annealing at high temperatures ( > 500 ° C. ) will be required to achieve a high quality film [ Reference no . 7 ] .
[ 0007 ] In addition to B - Ga2O3 , which is the most stable polymorph of Ga203 , gallium oxide has a few other poly morphs that are metastable ; these include Y- , E- , K- , d- , and a - Ga_03 [ References no . 3 , 9-14 ] . Currently , the y poly morphs can only be obtained in specific process conditions ; meanwhile , information about the ? , K , and 8 polymorphs is
limited and , in some cases , debated in the literature [ Refer ences no . 11 , 12 ] mainly because these polymorphs are difficult to obtain as isolated phases which makes their structure determination challenging [ Reference no . 7 ] . On the other hand , the a - Ga203 metastable polymorph is the most studied and technologically appealing metastable poly morph due to its superior properties for both power handling and optoelectronics and its stability at ambient to high temperatures and pressures [ References no . 3 , 7 , 9 , 10 ) .
[ 0008 ] There remains a need in the art for methods for forming a high quality , thin film comprising B - Ga Oz on a non - native substrate , using an energy - efficient fabrication
process .

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
[ 0003 ] Power electronic devices are devices that convert DC power to AC power , or vice versa . For example , power electronic devices convert DC power generated by solar cells and fuel cells to AC power , thereby making it usable by consumers . As another example , power electronic devices convert AC power supplied by a provider to DC power , thereby making it usable for charging the battery of an
electric car or a portable electronic device . [ 0004 ] Research into new materials for power electronic devices has emerged as an inseparable part of sustainable development and efficient handling of electrical energy during the past three decades . Wide bandgap semiconduc tors such as GaN and SiC have been considered as candidate
materials for power devices to overcome the limitations of their traditional predecessors ( such as Si and GaAs ) in meeting the growing needs and the stringent requirements of the high energy demand society today . [ 0005 ] During the past few years , gallium oxide ( Ga , 02 ) has been proposed as an alternative material for such semi conductor devices promising to offer higher efficiency in power handling than the materials in use today and expected to compete with and complement the outstanding properties of GaN as the frontrunner material for power electronic devices [ References no . 1-5 ] . In addition to power applica tions , Ga , 0 , expands the wavelength span of optoelectronic devices to the deep UV [ Reference no . 3 ] . The properties of Gazoz depend on its crystal structure [ Reference no . 3 ) , and high quality films of crystalline forms of Ga203 , specifically of its most stable polymorph , are required for fabricating devices .
[ 0006 ] Therefore , most attention has been devoted to monoclinic ß - Ga203 as the most stable polymorph of Ga203 ( belonging to the space group C2 / m ) . With the recent availability of ß - Ga203 bulk wafers ( grown from the melt at high temperatures , ca. 1800 ° C. ) [ References no . 1 , 3-5 ] , homoepitaxial thin films of this Ga203 polymorph can be deposited on its native substrate [ References no . 1 , 3 , 4 ] . However , growing high quality B - Gazoz films on the native substrate ( i.e. , homoepitaxy ) is currently performed at high temperatures , ca. 600-800 ° C. , which consumes a lot of energy , and still only produces B - Ga_02 films on B - Ga_02 wafers that only allow for fabrication of very limited devices for limited applications [ References no . 1 , 2 ] . In addition , bulk B - Gazoz wafers have a low thermal conductivity which hinders the ability of ß - Ga203 devices to operate at their expected capabilities [ Reference no . 6 ] . Meanwhile , grow ing ß - Ga203 films on non - native substrates ( i.e. , heteroepi taxy ) is even more challenging ; it is only possible on very
[ 0009 ] The present invention involves using an epitaxial deposition process , such as plasma - enhanced atomic layer deposition , to form an intermediate buffer layer of a meta stable Ga2O3 , such as a - Ga2O3 , before depositing reactants that form the B - Ga_03 film on the buffer layer . In embodi ments , the process may be optimized to achieve crystallinity at a temperature of about 277 ° C. which is relatively low in the context of crystalline material growth . In embodiments , the process provides an energy - efficient fabrication process for growing ß - Ga203 films , with minimal inclusion of other Ga203 polymorphs , on non - native substrates on which an intermediate layer of metastable Gazoz can be grown .
[ 0010 ] In one aspect , the present invention comprises a method for forming a thin film comprising beta - gallium oxide ( ß - Ga203 ) on a substrate . The method uses an epi taxial deposition process comprising the steps of :
[ 0011 ] ( a ) depositing a buffer layer of metastable Gazoz on the substrate ; and
[ 0012 ] ( b ) reacting a gallium precursor with an oxygen precursor to deposit a layer comprising ß - Ga_03 on the buffer layer .
[ 0013 ] In embodiments of the method , the method further comprises repeating step ( b ) to deposit one or more addi tional layers comprising B - Ga Oz on a previously deposited layer comprising B - Ga_03 .
[ 0014 ] In embodiments of the method , the layer compris ing B - Gazoz comprises at least 90 % B - Ga2O3 , by ratio of mass of ß - Ga202 to mass of a - Ga203 and B - Ga203 , collec tively .
[ 0015 ] In embodiments of the method , the epitaxial depo sition process is an atomic layer deposition ( ALD ) process .
[ 0016 ] In embodiments of the method , the buffer layer is a single monolayer of metastable Ga203 . In embodiments of the method , the layer comprising B - Ga203 is a single mono layer comprising B - Ga203 .

[ 0043 ] " Atomic layer deposition ” or “ ALD ” is a subclass of chemical vapor deposition , used to deposit thin films onto a substrate . ALD typically involves the sequential use of gas phase reactants , and / or plasma phase reactants , and surface chemical processes .
[ 0044 ] “ Buffer layer " is one or more material layer ( s ) that provide an interface between a substrate underlying the buffer layer and an overlying film formed on the buffer layer .
[ 0045 ] “ Epitaxial deposition process ” , as used herein , refers to a process that involves placing a substrate in a reaction chamber , and introducing one or more precursor ( reactant ) materials into the reaction chamber , such that the precursor ( s ) or their reaction product ( s ) , deposit on the substrate to form a non - amorphous , crystalline layer having defined crystallographic orientation ( s ) relative to the under lying layer ( s ) . In non - limiting embodiments , the epitaxial deposition process may comprise chemical vapor deposition ( CVD ) processes , physical vapor deposition ( PVD ) pro cesses , or any other suitable deposition techniques as are known to a person skilled in the art of forming thin films . Chemical vapor deposition ( CVD ) processes may be per formed using a variety of techniques known to a person skilled in the art , with non - limiting embodiments including metal - organic CVD ( MOCVD ) , mist CVD , low pressure CVD , atmospheric CVD , plasma - assisted CVD ( also referred to as plasma - enhanced CVD ) , photo - assisted CVD , molecular layer deposition ( MLD ) , and atomic layer depo sition ( ALD ) including spatial ALD , thermal ALD , plasma assisted ALD ( also referred to as plasma - enhanced ALD ) , and photo - assisted ALD . Metal - organic vapor phase epitaxy ( MOVPE ) , halide vapor phase epitaxy ( HVPE ) and liquid phase epitaxy ( LPE ) may also be used . Physical vapor deposition ( PVD ) processes may be performed using a variety of sputtering techniques known to a person skilled in the art , with non - limiting embodiments including ion beam deposition , reactive sputtering , magnetron sputtering , and RF diode sputtering . Physical vapor deposition ( PVD ) pro cesses may also be performed using a variety of evaporation techniques known to a person skilled in the art , with non - limiting embodiments including thermal evaporation , e - beam evaporation , pulsed laser deposition ( PLD ) , and molecular beam epitaxy ( MBE ) including reactive MBE .

This method is referred to herein as the “ buffer - mediated Ga203 deposition process ” . In one embodiment , the buffer - mediated Ga , O3 deposition process uses an epitaxial deposition process comprising the following steps :
[ 0054 ] ( a ) depositing a buffer layer of metastable Ga_03 on a substrate ; [ 0055 ] ( b ) reacting a gallium precursor ( e.g. , triethylgal lium ( TEG ) gas ) with an oxygen precursor ( e.g. , oxygen plasma ) to deposit a layer of B - Ga O , on the buffer layer ;
and
[ 0056 ] ( c ) repeating step ( b ) to deposit additional layers of B - Ga , 0 , on previously deposited layers of ß - Ga , 03 .
[ 0057 ] In one non - limiting embodiment , the substrate is a GaN - compatible substrate . In one embodiment , the GaN compatible substrate is sapphire , and more particularly c - plane sapphire . In embodiments , the metastable Ga , 0 may be any one of the a - Ga , 03 , Y - Ga , 03 , E - Ga , 03 , K - Ga , 03 , and 8 - Gazoz polymorphs . [ 0066 ] In embodiments of the GaN - mediated a - Ga203 deposition process , the epitaxial deposition process is plasma - enhanced ALD .
[ 0067 ] In embodiments of the GaN - mediated a - Ga203 deposition process , each deposited layer of w - GaN , gallium
precursor , and nitrogen precursor , and a - Ga2O3 is a mono layer .
[ 0068 ] In embodiments of the GaN - mediated a - Ga203 deposition process , the process may be performed at a deposition temperature less than about 500 ° C. , and prefer ably less than about 300 ° C. , such as 277 ° C.
[ 0069 ] In embodiments of the GaN - mediated a - Ga_03 deposition process , step ( a ) is preceded by pretreating the
substrate with N / H , forming gas plasma to remove con tamination and pretreat the surface prior to deposition .
[ 0070 ] In embodiments of the GaN - mediated a - Ga 03 deposition process , sub - steps ( a ) ( i ) and ( a ) ( ii ) and step ( b ) may comprise providing pulsed doses of the gallium pre cursor , nitrogen precursor and oxygen precursor , respec
tively , into the reaction chamber in which the epitaxial deposition process is performed .
[ 0071 ] In embodiments of the GaN - mediated a - Ga203 deposition process , introduction of the gallium precursor and the nitrogen precursor into the reaction chamber is sequential , and the nitrogen precursor reacts with the first gallium precursor layer on the surface of the substrate . In other embodiments ( e.g. , using chemical vapor deposition ) , the introduction of the gallium precursor and the nitrogen precursor into the reaction chamber may be simultaneous to form the first layer of w - GaN on the substrate . In either case , the formed layer of w - GaN provides a highly symmetric atomic scale scaffold of gallium atoms , but is sacrificed in the following step to form the layer of a - Ga203 on the
substrate .
[ 0072 ] In embodiments of the GaN - mediated a - Ga203 deposition process , any one of sub - steps ( a ) ( i ) or ( a ) ( ii ) or step ( b ) may be followed by purging the reaction chamber in which the epitaxial deposition process is performed with an inert gas ( e.g. , argon gas ) to remove any excess of the gallium precursor , nitrogen precursor , or oxygen precursor ( as the case may be ) and / or reaction byproducts from the
reaction chamber .

[ 0076 ] In one non - limiting embodiment as shown in part of FIG . 8 , the Ga Oz deposition process uses an epitaxial deposition process comprising the following steps :
[ 0077 ] ( a ) depositing a layer of triethylgallium ( TEG ) gas on the buffer layer ; [ 0078 ] ( b ) reacting the layer of TEG with oxygen plasma to deposit a layer of Ga203 on the buffer layer ; and [ 0079 ] ( c ) repeating the foregoing steps ( a ) and ( b ) to create additional layers of Ga Oz on previously deposited layer ( s ) of Ga203 . [ 0080 ] In embodiments of the Ga203 deposition process , epitaxial deposition process is plasma - enhanced ALD . [ 0081 ] In embodiments of the Ga203 deposition process , each deposited layer of TEG , oxygen plasma , and Ga203 is a monolayer .
[ 0082 ] In embodiments of the Ga203 deposition process , the process may be performed at a deposition temperature less than about 500 ° C. , and preferably less than about 300 ° C. , such as 277 ° C.
[ 0083 ] In embodiments of the Ga203 deposition process , step ( a ) may be preceded by pretreating the substrate with oxygen plasma to remove contamination and pretreat the surface prior to deposition . [ 0084 ] In embodiments of the Ga2O3 deposition process , steps ( a ) and ( b ) comprise providing pulsed doses of TEG and the oxygen plasma , respectively , into the reaction cham ber in which the epitaxial deposition process is performed . [ 0085 ] In embodiments of the Ga203 deposition process , any one of steps ( a ) or ( b ) may be followed by purging the reaction chamber in which the epitaxial deposition process is performed with an inert gas ( e.g. , argon gas ) to remove any excess of the TEG , or oxygen plasma , and / or reaction byproducts from the reaction chamber .

[ 0109 ] In summary , the present invention provides an epitaxial deposition process that allows for formation of a highly oriented , crystalline B - Ga203 film on a substrate , which may even be a non - native substrate ( and more par ticularly , a GaN - compatible substrate ) at a low thermal budget ( i.e. , at temperatures that are hundreds of degrees lower than the processes currently in use for B - Ga_03 deposition ) .

Accordingly , the crystalline Ga_03 film formed by the present invention may be predominantly of the ß - Ga 03 polymorph , with minimal inclusion of other Ga203 polymorphs . [ 0111 ] The present invention makes the development of Ga203 semiconductor heterostructures and integration of Ga , 03 with existing semiconductor device components on a monolithic substrate possible and facilitates fast - track devel opment of Ga_02 electronics . Development of a low tem perature technology for B - Ga , 03 growth ( specially a GaN compatible one ) as a result of the present invention is a key enabling technology for wide bandgap semiconductors lead ing to energy - efficient electronic devices , not only in per formance but also an energy - efficient fabrication process . Fabrication of Ga203 devices on non - native substrates using the present invention also allows for the transfer of pertinent thermal management technologies that are already estab
lished for wide bandgap electronics [ Reference no . 16 ) , which will mitigate the low thermal conductivity of Ga_03 and make devices available that are able to concurrently handle higher power , higher voltage , and higher operating temperatures .
